mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and subsequently drives up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where GDP growth rate is above 3%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives down the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where the federal funds rate is above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to decreased consumer spending and subsequently drives down the S&P 500 index over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where the unemployment rate is rising.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates an increase in economic activity, which leads to higher demand for goods and services, driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where industrial production is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP growth rate and housing starts are increasing, it signals a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher economic growth and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where both GDP growth rate and housing starts are increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 2% and the CPI is increasing, it signals an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where the federal funds rate is below 2% and the CPI is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is low and payroll employment is increasing, it signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where the unemployment rate is low and payroll employment is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production is increasing and housing starts are strong, it signals an increase in economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where industrial production is increasing and housing starts are strong.
